arxiv-2004-04225.title: Measuring Emotions in the COVID-19 Real World Worry Dataset
arxiv-2004-04225.creator: Bennett Kleinberg, Isabelle van der Vegt, Maximilian Mozes
arxiv-2004-04225.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic is having a dramatic impact on societies and economies around the world. With various measures of lockdowns and social distancing in place, it becomes important to understand emotional responses on a large scale. In this paper, we present the first ground truth dataset of emotional responses to COVID-19.

arxiv-2103-06063.title: On spatial variation in the detectability and density of social media user protest supporters
arxiv-2103-06063.creator: Víctor H. Masías, Fernando Crespo, Pilar Navarro R, Razan Masood, Nicole C. Krämer, H. Ulrich Hoppe
arxiv-2103-06063.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Víctor H. Masías, Fernando Crespo, Pilar Navarro R, Razan Masood, Nicole C. Krämer, H. Ulrich Hoppe. Although much has been published regarding street protests on social media, few works have attempted to characterize social media users’ spatial behavior in such events. The research reported here uses spatial capture-recapture methods to determine the influence of the built environment, physical proximity to protest location, and collective posting rhythm on variations in users’ spatial detectability and density during a protest in Mexico City.

arxiv-2204-11373.title: Entity-Conditioned Question Generation for Robust Attention Distribution in Neural Information Retrieval Conference: Proceedings of the 45th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2022; Madrid, Spain Proceedings of the 45th International
arxiv-2204-11373.creator: Revanth Reddy, Md Arafat Sultan, Martin Franz, Avirup Sil, Heng Ji
arxiv-2204-11373.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Revanth Reddy, Md Arafat Sultan, Martin Franz, Avirup Sil, Heng Ji. We show that supervised neural information retrieval (IR) models are prone to learning sparse attention patterns over passage tokens, which can result in key phrases including named entities receiving low attention weights, eventually leading to model under-performance.

arxiv-2407-00583.title: Closure Invariants for Polarised Radio Interferometric Observations: a graph theoretical approach
arxiv-2407-00583.creator: Vinay Kumar 1⋆, Rajaram Nityananda 1†, Joseph Samuel 1,2‡
arxiv-2407-00583.description: Abstract Aperture synthesis observations with full polarisation have long been used to study the magnetic fields of synchrotron emitting sources. Recently proposed closure invariants give us a powerful method for extracting information from measured visibilities which are corrupted by antenna and polarisation dependent gains.

arxiv-2410-21762.title: Adjacent cycle-chains are e e -positive
arxiv-2410-21762.creator: Foster Tom, Aarush Vailaya
arxiv-2410-21762.description: Abstract We describe a way to decompose the chromatic symmetric function as a positive sum of smaller pieces. We show that these pieces are e e -positive for cycles. Then we prove that attaching a cycle to a graph preserves the e e -positivity of these pieces.

pmc-10483754.title: Using big data and Population Health Management to assess care and costs for patients with severe mental disorders and move toward a value-based payment system
pmc-10483754.creator: Valeria D Tozzi, Helen Banks, Lucia Ferrara, Angelo Barbato, Giovanni Corrao, Barbara D’avanzo, Teresa Di Fiandra, Andrea Gaddini, Matteo Monzio Compagnoni, Michele Sanza, Alessio Saponaro, Salvatore Scondotto, Antonio Lora
pmc-10483754.description: BackgroundMental health (MH) care often exhibits uneven quality and poor coordination of physical and MH needs, especially for patients with severe mental disorders. This study tests a Population Health Management (PHM) approach to identify patients with severe mental disorders using administrative health databases in Italy and evaluate, manage and monitor care pathways and costs.

pmc-11510521.title: Acute Retinal Necrosis Associated with Epstein–Barr Virus Successfully Treated with Antiviral Treatment: A Case Report
pmc-11510521.creator: Heejeong You, Joonhyung Kim
pmc-11510521.description: Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is a rare cause of acute retinal necrosis (ARN) and is known for its poor prognosis and limited response to conventional antiviral treatment. Herein, we report a case of EBV ARN successfully treated with conventional systemic acyclovir and intravitreal ganciclovir injection. An 85-year-old man presented with visual disturbance of the right eye from 10 days prior.

pmc-11530602.title: Local crime and substance use disorders: A comparison of midlife adults in the 1990s and 2000s☆
pmc-11530602.creator: Jennifer W. Robinette, Jason D. Boardman, Kathleen Mullan Harris
pmc-11530602.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study investigated how sociopolitical changes in the United States between the 1990s and 2000s may explain the increase in substance use disorders and reduced longevity in more recent cohorts of US midlife adults. The 2008 recession which drastically increased unemployment rates across the country may have had negative implications for downstream contextual and individual processes, including both local crime rates and substance use disorders.

pmc-11541839.title: Derived cannabinoid product availability among online vape shops
pmc-11541839.creator: Nora Satybaldiyeva, Raquel Harati, Tomas Mejorado, Nicolas Morales, Gustavo Benitez, Shannon E. Ellis, Karen Ferran, Eric C. Leas
pmc-11541839.description: Highlights•Nearly 36% of vape shops in San Diego, California sold derived cannabinoid products.•About 27% of vape shops sold flavored and inhalable derived cannabinoid products.•California’s Assembly Bill 45 prohibits flavored & inhalable derived cannabinoid sale.•Vape shops that sold derived cannabinoid products received more website visits.

pmc-11606215.title: Towards a risk assessment framework for micro- and nanoplastic particles for human health
pmc-11606215.creator: Amelie Vogel, Jutta Tentschert, Raymond Pieters, Francesca Bennet, Hubert Dirven, Annemijne van den Berg, Esther Lenssen, Maartje Rietdijk, Dirk Broßell, Andrea Haase
pmc-11606215.description: BackgroundHuman exposure to micro- and nanoplastic particles (MNPs) is inevitable but human health risk assessment remains challenging for several reasons. MNPs are complex mixtures of particles derived from different polymer types, which may contain plenty of additives and/or contaminants. MNPs cover broad size distributions and often have irregular shapes and morphologies.

pmc-11638478.title: The Relationship Between Cognitive Emotion Regulation Strategy and Mental Health Among University Students During Public Health Emergency: A Network Analysis
pmc-11638478.creator: Mengze Li, Qiannan Jia, Tifei Yuan, Lin Zhang, Huizhong Wang, Jamie Ward, Yinchuan Jin, Qun Yang
pmc-11638478.description: BackgroundPublic health emergencies pose threats to mental health, and cognitive emotional regulation can be a crucial coping strategy. This study explored the relationship between cognitive emotion regulation strategies and mental health among university students during the COVID-19 pandemic using network analysis.Methods1100 university students completed questionnaires assessing depression, anxiety, somatization, and cognitive emotion regulation strategies.

pmc-12491742.title: Disentangling unobserved heterogeneity: Novel application of a statistical method to evaluate a multilevel healthcare intervention for hispanic individuals living on the United States-Mexico border with comorbid diabetes and hypertension
pmc-12491742.creator: MinJae Lee, Juliana Z. Lopez, Natalia I. Heredia, Maria Zolezzi, Soo Kyung Park, Paul G. Yeh, Lisa Mitchell-Bennett, Belinda M. Reininger
pmc-12491742.description: ObjectiveIndividuals with diabetes and hypertension represent a high-risk population with poor prognosis and high healthcare costs. Clinicians recognize the complexities of treating patients with multiple chronic conditions; however, the research literature shows little attention to characterizing change patterns in hypertension outcomes for participants of health interventions.

pmc-12751475.title: Efficacy and safety of periodontal initial therapy combined with intralesional betamethasone sodium phosphate injection under local anesthesia in managing erosive oral lichen planus: study protocol for a multi-center, split-mouth, randomized self-controlled trial
pmc-12751475.creator: Huiwen Chen, Liran Shi, Qianhui Shang, Zihao Wei, Qiaozhen Yang, Yining He, Chenxi Li, Zengtong Zhou, Guoyao Tang, Hongying Sun, Gulinuer Awuti, Zhongchen Song, Linjun Shi
pmc-12751475.description: IntroductionErosive oral lichen planus (OLP) and periodontitis frequently coexist and may worsen each other. This study will evaluate the effectiveness and safety of combining periodontal initial therapy under local anesthesia with intralesional betamethasone sodium phosphate (BSP) injection in patients with erosive OLP, particularly in enhancing lesion healing.Methods and analysisThis is a multicenter, randomized, split-mouth, self-controlled trial.

pmc-13230876.title: An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health record data
pmc-13230876.creator: Yanfei Wang, Yongqiu Li, Tuo Lin, Yi Guo
pmc-13230876.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Target trial emulation (TTE) enables causal inference from electronic health record (EHR) data when randomized clinical trials are infeasible, but its validity depends on whether EHR data can support the required trial design components.

pmc-13283904.title: A Rare Coexistence: Uterine Leiomyoma Arising in a Mature Cystic Teratoma and a Pedunculated Endometriotic Cyst Mimicking Leiomyoma—Two Case Reports
pmc-13283904.creator: Mena Abdalla, Victoria Barker, Anitha Nayar, Sahathevan Sathiyathasan, Adjoa Appiah, Ibrahim ElHag, Alexander Steshenko, Saira Khan, Arjun Anilkumar, Aisha Hameed

pmc-13422059.title: Severe Hypertriglyceridaemia-Induced Necrotising Pancreatitis Complicated by Multi-organ Failure: A Case Report
pmc-13422059.creator: Aharabie Jeyabavan, Guillaume Lambert, Nadeem M Sabir
pmc-13422059.description: We report a case of a woman in her 30s presenting with severe epigastric pain and vomiting. Initial laboratory analysis was significantly delayed due to marked lipaemia. Subsequent investigations revealed an elevated serum amylase (2636 IU/L) and markedly raised fasting triglycerides (20.4 mmol/L).

pmc-13524465.title: Gut Faecalibacterium regulates host immunity and metabolic profiles to confer resistance against Salmonella infection in chicks
pmc-13524465.creator: Xiang Li, Yaping Wang, Zixuan Wang, Man Deng, Jumei Zheng, He Geng, Guiping Zhao, Qiao Wang
pmc-13524465.description: To explore the pathogenic mechanism of Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) infection in chicks and the regulatory role of Faecalibacterium, we established a chick SE infection model, systematically analyzing intestinal damage, systemic inflammation, and cecal microbial community changes. Focusing on the differentially abundant Faecalibacterium, we elucidated its regulatory mechanism via metagenomics, transcriptomics, and serum metabolomics.

pmc-13536628.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals compartment-specific cytotoxic T cell crosstalk with AT2 and goblet cells in advanced COPD
pmc-13536628.creator: Ayu Hutami Syarif, Bernhard F E Reiter, Alexander Avian, Katrin Milger, Elena Ellmeier, Gerald Hoefler, Clemens Aigner, Alberto Benazzo, Sophia Auner, Slaven Crnkovic, Stefano Angiari, Francesca Polverino, Grazyna Kwapiszewska, Leigh M Marsh

pmc-13560418.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of IgA nephropathy and comorbid diabetic kidney disease
pmc-13560418.creator: Anni Wang, Wen Shi, Kunyue Xu, Yuan Yuan, Xuanli Tang, Shuman Zhao, Dongrong Yu, Hong Liu, Xiang Liu, Xue Jiang
pmc-13560418.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsThis study characterized clinical features, pathology, treatment, and prognosis of biopsy-confirmed coexisting IgA nephropathy (IgAN) and diabetic kidney disease (DKD).MethodsThis single-centre retrospective study included 80 patients with biopsy-proven IgAN + DKD (2010–2023). Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to establish comparable groups of IgAN (n = 80) and DKD (n = 80), matched on age, sex and baseline serum creatinine (sCr).

pmc-13670397.title: Impact of Plant Pre‐Processing on the Chemical Profile of Psidium guajava L. (Myrtaceae) Essential Oil and Evaluation of Its Bioactive Potential
pmc-13670397.creator: Tarsila da C Silva, Ari Sérgio de O Lemos, Caio Juan S Fortes, Débora N Eiriz, Elaine S Coimbra, Lucas de A Carvalho, Luciana M Chedier, Lucas M Duarte, Núbia B Andrade, Rodrigo L Fabri, Selma R de Paiva, Alessandra L Valverde
pmc-13670397.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The chemical composition and bioactivity of essential oils depend not only on agronomic and environmental factors but also on the pre‐processing of the plant material, a step that is rarely evaluated. Leaf essential oils of Psidium guajava L. were obtained by hydrodistillation from fresh or previously frozen leaves fragmented manually or mechanically, and assessed for GC‐MS composition, cytotoxicity and biological activities.
